risks.title: Exit depends on a tenancy renewal that has not happened
risks.message: The broker states the exit is 'refinance once the purchase has settled and the tenancy is renewed'. The exit therefore depends on a future event: the tenancy renewal. The letter does not say how many tenants there are, when the current lease ends, or how far renewal negotiations have progressed. If renewal is to a single tenant, this is also single-tenant reliance. The credit submission must explain this risk and what happens if the lease is not renewed.

risks.title: Refinance exit not shown to meet mainstream criteria
risks.message: The exit is a refinance after 24 months, but the application gives no basis for showing a mainstream lender would accept the loan at that point. It omits income, lease terms, tenant details and serviceability, and refinance appears to depend on the renewed tenancy. The credit submission should show the loan would meet a mainstream lender's criteria at the end of the term.

risks.title: Who commissioned the pending valuation is unclear
risks.message: The broker says a formal valuation 'has been ordered' but does not say who ordered it or which valuer. If the borrower or broker commissioned it rather than a panel valuer instructed for the Lender, it can be used for initial assessment only.
